newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, mobile industry unite on new technology.
newsitem.headline: EU, mobile industry unite on new technology.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it was working with European companies to develop a strategy for introducing the next generation of mobile communications technology.
The European Union executive said the two sides would promote the Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS), a technology that will allow advanced mobile multimedia systems to be developed.

"Industry agreed to provide within the next months its common vision and detailed regulatory requirements for UMTS," the Commission said in a statement that reported on a meeting between the companies and Telecommunications Commissioner Martin Bangemann.

The Commission noted that European companies had developed the worldwide GSM digital mobile phone standard and were well placed to promote the new technology, which will allow consumers to carry out a range of data and video communications over small "personal communicators".

The industry leaders told the Commission they needed a stable regulatory environment, including licensing conditions and dedicated frequency allocations. The Commission said a key role would be played by the new UMTS Forum, which unites manufacturers, cellular and satellite communications operators, regulators and others.
